title: Four early signs of creative fatigue, and the refresh-or-cut call
hook: An ad shows it is tiring before the cost per order moves. Four early signs to watch.
caption:
An ad shows it is tiring before the cost per order moves. Four early signs to watch.

Fewer people stay past the opening. The same people see it more often. Clicks drop while spend holds. Comments start saying “seen this”.

Then ask one question: is the message tired, or only the look?

If the message still works in other ads, refresh the look. In our analysis, a proven message in a new look got 47% more first-month spend.

Save the Monday check on the last slide. Follow @galvor.ai.

slides.headline: Is the *message* tired, or only the *look*?
slides.body:
Check other ads carrying the same message.

If they still hold, the message is fine and this ad's look has worn out. If they are all slipping, the message itself needs a rest.

notes:
Reader: a media buyer or growth lead who watches ad performance weekly. One argument: fatigue has early signs, and the useful decision is whether the message or only the look is worn. Numbers used: 47% more first-month spend for a proven message in a new look (facts bank, Decoded #3; second and last use in this group). The four signs are common practice and carry no thresholds on purpose, since the facts bank has none. First comment points to Decoded #6 (Creative Fatigue), published 25 Nov. Topic kept and sharpened.
